title: A safer, simpler workspace invite flow
summary: Invite teammates by email with single-use links and a clear audit trail. Reuse the existing sign-in flow, make delivery recoverable, and roll out gradually.

objects.title: Make invite links single-use
objects.summary: Use hashed tokens that expire after 72 hours. Redeem the token and create membership in one transaction.
objects.context: An invite grants access to a workspace. Reusable or concurrently redeemed links could give unintended access.
objects.rationale: Server-side state supports revocation and atomic consumption. Storing a hash limits exposure if the database is read.

alternatives.title: Signed JWT invitations
alternatives.tradeoff: Avoids a token lookup, but revocation and single use still require server-side state.

consequences: Accepting an invite requires a database transaction.
Admins need a resend path for expired invitations.

objects.title: Decouple email from the request
objects.summary: Write an email outbox record alongside the invite, then deliver through the existing job queue.
objects.context: Email provider outages should not prevent an admin from creating an invitation.
objects.rationale: The invite and its email job commit together. A stable invite ID makes retries idempotent.

alternatives.title: Send email inline
alternatives.tradeoff: Less moving code, but the admin request depends on email provider availability.

consequences: The worker needs an idempotent retry policy.

objects.title: A verified email identifies the invitee
objects.summary: Confirm how email aliases and enterprise SSO accounts map to the provider’s verified email before building acceptance.

objects.title: Two requests could redeem one invite
objects.summary: Enforce unique workspace membership and consume tokens atomically. Test concurrent requests explicitly.

objects.title: Add the invite data model
objects.summary: Create token, expiry, inviter, workspace, and outbox fields. Enforce unique workspace membership.

objects.title: Build creation and acceptance endpoints
objects.summary: Validate admin access, verified email, workspace scope, token expiry, and single use.

objects.title: Build the admin invite experience
objects.summary: Add an invite dialog, pending invites, resend action, and clear acceptance states.

objects.title: Test the edges. Roll out gradually.
objects.summary: Cover concurrency, expired links, workspace isolation, and retries. Enable internal workspaces first.

objects.title: Committed invites remain recoverable
objects.summary: A committed invitation always has an email job; retrying delivery does not create another invite.

objects.title: Is 72 hours enough for enterprise teams?
objects.summary: Weekend delays could make onboarding frustrating. Consider configurable expiry or a low-friction resend path.

objects.title: Invitation API
objects.summary: Creates invitations and validates acceptance. Commits invitation and email outbox records together.

objects.title: Email outbox
objects.summary: Stores the email job alongside the invitation so committed invitations remain recoverable.

objects.title: Email worker
objects.summary: Delivers invitations through the existing job queue and retries using the invite ID as its idempotency key.

reviewFocus: Is a 72-hour invite lifetime practical for enterprise onboarding, or should admins be able to configure it?
Can the identity provider reliably match an invite to a verified email, including aliases and SSO accounts?
Do atomic token consumption and the email outbox cover concurrent requests and delivery failures?

diagrams.title: Invitation delivery architecture
diagrams.description: The API records the invitation and its email job together. The existing worker handles delivery and retries independently of the admin request.

relationshipMap.title: Dependencies
relationshipMap.description: Inspect how token storage, API delivery, and rollout prerequisites affect this change.
